title: Arbitrary-ring polynomial graph diagonal class and scalar extension
statement:
Let $R\to B$ be a flat finitely presented homomorphism of arbitrary commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], and fix $n\geq0$ and a surjection $P=R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\twoheadrightarrow B$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Work in ordinary unbounded module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with derived coinduction $C_D^E=R\operatorname{Hom}_E(D,-)$ and its precomposition action [def-trf-derived-coinduction], [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], and derived tensor [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor]. Put $L=\Omega^n_{P/R}[n]$, $C=C_B^P(L)$, $Q=B_1\otimes_RB_2$, $p_1(b)=b\otimes1$, $C_1=C\otimes_{B,p_1}^{\mathbf L}Q$, and let $\delta:Q\to B$ be multiplication [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], [def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra], [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Set $T=P\otimes_RB_2$, $q:T\to Q$, and $e=\delta q:T\to B$, $t_i\mapsto\bar t_i$. The evaluation-counit exchange for the flat extension $R\to B_2$ identifies $C_1$ with $C_Q^T(\Omega^n_{T/B_2}[n])$ [lem-sfb-perfect-coinduction-tor-independent-exchange]. The normalized diagonal isomorphism of [def-sfb-polynomial-koszul-diagonal-data] exists over these arbitrary rings:
$$\kappa_P:C_B^Q(C_1)\xrightarrow{\sim}C_B^T(\Omega^n_{T/B_2}[n])\xrightarrow{\sim}B[0].$$
The first map uses that exchange and the coinduction-transitivity comparison with composite evaluation counit. The second is the ordered graph Koszul trace for $t_i-\bar t_i$, sending the dual top graph wedge paired with $dt_1\wedge\cdots\wedge dt_n$ to $1$, with the cohomological tensor signs. Let $\xi_P:B[0]\to C_1$ in $D(Q)$ be the coinduction adjunct of $\kappa_P^{-1}$. Its multiplication map $B\to R\operatorname{Hom}_Q(B,C_1)$ is an isomorphism.
For every homomorphism $R\to R'$ of arbitrary commutative rings put $B'=B\otimes_RR'$, $P'=P\otimes_RR'$, $Q'=B'\otimes_{R'}B'$, $L'=\Omega^n_{P'/R'}[n]$, $C'=C_{B'}^{P'}(L')$, and $C'_1=C'\otimes_{B',p'_1}^{\mathbf L}Q'$. Let $c:C\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}B'\xrightarrow{\sim}C'$ be the evaluation-counit exchange, with the coefficient map carrying the ordered volume to the ordered volume. Under $B\otimes_Q^{\mathbf L}Q'\simeq B'$, let $d:C_1\otimes_Q^{\mathbf L}Q'\to C'_1$ be induced by $c$ and the tensor associators. Then
$$d\circ(\xi_P\otimes_Q^{\mathbf L}Q')=\xi_{P'}.$$
The equality preserves the specified class itself, respects identity and successive base extensions, and includes the empty tuple and zero rings. Neither ring is assumed Noetherian, $R\to R'$ need not be flat, and $B$ is not assumed perfect over its self-product $Q$. No proper scheme, proper-adjoint comparison, or trace-pair base-change map is part of this assertion.

source.place: Agent arbitrary-ring scalar clause of Tag 0E2E (lemma-relative-dualizing-noetherian), with Tag 0E2F (lemma-base-change-relative-dualizing), Tags 0A70/0A71 (lemma-right-adjoint, lemma-RHom-ext), and ordered volume convention of Tag 0BZI (section-relative-dualizing-complex-algebraic). Exact normalized-class compatibility is an agent enhancement of the generator claim of 0E2F.

proof.text: First fix the coefficient identifications. The universal property of differentials gives $\Omega_{P/R}=\bigoplus_iP\,dt_i$: a derivation is uniquely specified by its values on the $t_i$, and the inverse sends $(m_i)$ to $f\mapsto\sum_i(\partial f/\partial t_i)m_i$. The free exterior-basis formula of [lem-weil-pbc-exterior-power-free-basis] identifies $\Omega^n_{P/R}$ with $Pv$, $v=dt_1\wedge\cdots\wedge dt_n$. Over $T=B_2[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ and over every scalar extension use the identical formula, so the coefficient comparison carries $v$ to the ordered target volume. These maps preserve identities and composites on each $dt_i$, hence on the top wedge. Also $P$ is $R$-flat: on the monomial decomposition tensoring is a direct sum of copies of the original map. Tensoring with $T=P\otimes_RB$ or $Q=B\otimes_RB$ is successive tensoring with flat modules, hence preserves injections. Thus $P,T,Q,B$ are $R$-flat. This argument uses only finite-support polynomial expressions and applies to zero rings and $n=0$.

source.place: Agent ordered-volume/counit refinement of Tags 0E2E and 0E2F; Tag 0A70 (lemma-right-adjoint), Tag 0A71 (lemma-RHom-ext), lemma-composition-right-adjoints; polynomial volume convention in Tag 0BZI (section-relative-dualizing-complex-algebraic).

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-arbitrary-polynomial-dual-properties], $B[0]$ is perfect over $P$ without Noetherian hypotheses. The extension $P\to T=P\otimes_RB_2$ is flat: for a $P$-module $M$, $M\otimes_PT=M\otimes_RB_2$, so exactness is [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact]. In particular $B$ and $T$ are Tor independent over $P$ and $B\otimes_PT=Q$. Apply [lem-sfb-perfect-coinduction-tor-independent-exchange] to $P\to B$, $P\to T$, and $L$ to obtain the isomorphism $\beta:C_1\xrightarrow{\sim}C_Q^T(V_T[n])$, $V_T=T v$. Its normalization is exactly extension of the evaluation-at-one counit with the coefficient map in step 1. Thus it is the exchange specified in the statement, rather than an arbitrary isomorphism of the underlying objects.

source.place: Agent ordered-volume/counit refinement of Tags 0E2E and 0E2F; Tag 0A70 (lemma-right-adjoint), Tag 0A71 (lemma-RHom-ext), lemma-composition-right-adjoints; polynomial volume convention in Tag 0BZI (section-relative-dualizing-complex-algebraic).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-polynomial-graph-coinduction] with coefficient ring $B_2$, variables $t_i$, and evaluations $\bar t_i$. It gives the augmented bounded finite-free resolution $K_T(t_i-\bar t_i)\to B[0]$. Therefore [lem-sfb-koszul-evaluation-pasting] gives $\tau:C_B^T(V_T[n])\xrightarrow{\sim}B[0]$, sending the dual ordered top wedge paired with $v$ to $1$. The coinduction adjunctions of [lem-trf-derived-coinduction-adjunction] and right-adjoint composition [lem-cat-right-adjoint-composition] give $\alpha:C_B^Q C_Q^T\xrightarrow{\sim}C_B^T$, with composite evaluation counit. Define $\kappa=\tau\alpha C_B^Q(\beta)$. Each factor is invertible. Its counit and top-wedge normalizations are precisely those of [def-sfb-polynomial-koszul-diagonal-data], so this constructs the required normalized $\kappa_P$. No Koszul blocks have been permuted.

source.place: Agent ordered-volume/counit refinement of Tags 0E2E and 0E2F; Tag 0A70 (lemma-right-adjoint), Tag 0A71 (lemma-RHom-ext), lemma-composition-right-adjoints; polynomial volume convention in Tag 0BZI (section-relative-dualizing-complex-algebraic).

proof.text: Let $a=\kappa^{-1}:B[0]\to C_B^Q(C_1)$. Under the restriction/coinduction adjunction its adjunct is $\xi=\epsilon^\delta_{C_1}\circ\operatorname{Res}_\delta(a)$, as required. The multiplication map of this class is $a$: the precomposition action sends $b$ to the Hom class $x\mapsto\xi(bx)$, which is exactly the $B$-linear adjunct of $\xi$ because the counit is evaluation at $1$. This formula is the adjunction formula on K-injective representatives, and naturality of the adjunction gives it for the localized arrow $a$ as well. Thus the specified multiplication map is an isomorphism, since $a$ is.

source.place: Agent ordered-volume/counit refinement of Tags 0E2E and 0E2F; Tag 0A70 (lemma-right-adjoint), Tag 0A71 (lemma-RHom-ext), lemma-composition-right-adjoints; polynomial volume convention in Tag 0BZI (section-relative-dualizing-complex-algebraic).

proof.text: Now fix arbitrary $R\to R'$. The algebra $B'$ is $R'$-flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-base-change], and tensoring a finite generators-and-relations presentation of $B$ gives a finite presentation of $B'$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Put $T'=T\otimes_RR'$, canonically $P'\otimes_{R'}B'_2$, and $Q'=Q\otimes_RR'$. For any $X\in\{B,Q\}$ considered as a $T$-module, [lem-sfb-flat-algebra-derived-module-tensor-exchange] for the flat algebra $T/R$ identifies the restriction of $X\otimes_T^{\mathbf L}T'$ with $X\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R'$. Since $X$ is $R$-flat by step 1, the latter is $(X\otimes_RR')[0]$: tensor a free $R$-resolution of $R'$ with $X$ and use [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact]. This proves Tor independence for $T\to Q$, $T\to B$ after $T\to T'$. The same calculation for the flat algebras $P/R$ and $Q/R$ gives $B\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}P'\simeq B'$ and $B\otimes_Q^{\mathbf L}Q'\simeq B'$, with their canonical balancing maps. In particular the exchange of step 2 for $P\to P'$ gives exactly $c:C\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}B'\xrightarrow{\sim}C'$. No flatness of $R'$ over $R$ has been used.

source.place: Agent ordered-volume/counit refinement of Tags 0E2E and 0E2F; Tag 0A70 (lemma-right-adjoint), Tag 0A71 (lemma-RHom-ext), lemma-composition-right-adjoints; polynomial volume convention in Tag 0BZI (section-relative-dualizing-complex-algebraic).

proof.text:
Write $F$ for extension $D(Q)\to D(Q')$ and $G$ for extension $D(B)\to D(B')$, and set $H=C_B^Q(C_1)$, $E=C_B^T(V_T[n])$. Let $j:H\to E$ be the composite before $\tau$ in step 3, and let $j'$ be its primed version. Denote by $\gamma_\delta:G H\to C_{B'}^{Q'}(F C_1)$ the counit exchange, which exists by [lem-sfb-perfect-coinduction-tor-independent-exchange] even though $B$ need not be perfect over $Q$. Let $\gamma_e:G E\to C_{B'}^{T'}(V_{T'}[n])$ be the graph exchange. Then
$$j'\, C_{B'}^{Q'}(d)\,\gamma_\delta=\gamma_e\,G(j).$$
Indeed paste the two restriction/coinduction squares for $T\to Q\to B$ using clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting]; [lem-cat-right-adjoint-composition] identifies their pasted counit with that for $e$. For the remaining quotient square, the exchanges along $P\to T\to T'$ and $P\to P'\to T'$ agree by the successive-extension clause of [lem-sfb-perfect-coinduction-tor-independent-exchange]. The two tensor paths have the same balancing map on pure tensors and the same coefficient volume, so their mates identify $F\beta$ with $\beta'd$, inserting the $q$-exchange. Substituting this in the pasted identity gives the displayed equation. This uses existence, not invertibility, of $\gamma_\delta$.

source.place: Agent ordered-volume/counit refinement of Tags 0E2E and 0E2F; Tag 0A70 (lemma-right-adjoint), Tag 0A71 (lemma-RHom-ext), lemma-composition-right-adjoints; polynomial volume convention in Tag 0BZI (section-relative-dualizing-complex-algebraic).

proof.text:
The graph resolution in step 3 is finite free over $T$, and remains the augmented graph resolution after $T\to T'$; Tor independence was checked in step 5. Hence the scalar-extension clause of [lem-sfb-koszul-evaluation-pasting], with the ordered coefficient line identified in step 1, says $\tau'\gamma_e=G(\tau)$. Combining this with the equation of step 6 yields
$$\kappa'\,C_{B'}^{Q'}(d)\,\gamma_\delta=G(\kappa).$$
Consequently, for $a=\kappa^{-1}$ and $a'=(\kappa')^{-1}$,
$$C_{B'}^{Q'}(d)\,\gamma_\delta\,G(a)=a'.$$
This is equality of the normalized derived arrows, with no undetermined unit or orientation sign: the Koszul theorem preserves the ordered top functional itself, and scalar extension changes no degree or ordering.

proof.text: Take the adjunct of the last equation under $\operatorname{Res}_{\delta'}\dashv C_{B'}^{Q'}$. The defining equation for $\gamma_\delta$ is $\epsilon^{\delta'}\operatorname{Res}_{\delta'}(\gamma_\delta)=F(\epsilon^\delta)\theta_H$, where $\theta_H$ is the Tor-independent scalar/restriction comparison. Naturality of the counit with respect to $d$ and of $\theta$ with respect to $a$ identifies the adjunct of its left side with $d\,F(\epsilon^\delta\operatorname{Res}_\delta(a))=d\,F(\xi)$. Here $\theta_{B[0]}$ is the canonical $B\otimes_Q^{\mathbf L}Q'\simeq B'$ comparison checked in step 5, so the source is exactly the source fixed in the statement. The adjunct of the right side is $\xi'$. Bijectivity of adjunction therefore proves $d\circ(\xi_P\otimes_Q^{\mathbf L}Q')=\xi_{P'}$. This explicitly takes the mate, rather than asserting that an arbitrary generator is preserved.

proof.text: The identity and successive-extension clauses of [lem-sfb-perfect-coinduction-tor-independent-exchange] identify the direct and successive maps $c$, and hence their first-pullback maps $d$, under the canonical tensor associators. The analogous clauses of [lem-sfb-koszul-evaluation-pasting] identify the graph traces. Mate pasting preserves these identities, so steps 6--8 respect identity and successive extensions on the specified classes. If $n=0$, the graph tuple is empty, $T=B$, and its trace is the identity, as stated by [lem-trf-polynomial-graph-coinduction]; steps 2--8 still apply to the possibly nontrivial quotient $R\twoheadrightarrow B$. If a ring is zero all relevant module categories have only the zero object, and the formulas and invertible arrows above remain valid. The construction never invokes perfection of $B$ over $Q$, Noetherian approximation, or a proper-adjoint comparison.
